hook.line: Everyone reaches a point where asking nicely has stopped working. Spanish has a few ways to say you've reached it, and they get stronger as you go.

examples.es: Estoy harta de que siempre llegues tarde.
examples.en: I'm fed up with you always being late. (a woman speaking, to a friend)
I'm sick of waiting. (a man speaking)
I'm tired of saying it over and over.

examples.es: Estoy harto de que no me escuchen.
examples.en: I'm fed up with them not listening to me. (a man speaking)

rule:
Two frames after *estoy harto de*.

Same person feels and does: an infinitive. *Estoy harto de esperar.*

Someone else does it: *que* plus the wish form. *Estoy harta de que llegues tarde.*

*Harto* is for a man speaking, *harta* for a woman. English says "fed up with you being late"; Spanish needs *que*.

Milder: *Ya me cansé de…*. To cut it off: *¡Ya basta!* or *¡Ya basta de* plus the thing.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an expression of emotion: the feeling triggers the subjunctive after *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence: *Estoy harta de que siempre ___ tarde.* (*llegues* or *llegar*)
yourTurn.answer: Estoy harta de que siempre llegues tarde.
yourTurn.why: Someone else does it, so after *que* comes the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (a man speaking): I'm sick of waiting.
yourTurn.why: You do and feel it, so *de* plus an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm tired of saying it over and over.
yourTurn.why: *Ya me cansé de* plus an infinitive says "I've had it with".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (a woman speaking): I'm fed up with them not listening to me.
yourTurn.answer: Estoy harta de que no me escuchen.
yourTurn.why: A woman says *harta*, and *no me escuchen* is the wish form after *que*.
*Ya basta de* plus the thing you want stopped.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a woman speaking: *Estoy harto de esperar.*
yourTurn.why: *Harta* ends in *a* for a woman speaking.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about someone else: *Estoy harto de llegar tarde.* Say (a man speaking): I'm fed up with my brother being late.
yourTurn.answer: Estoy harto de que mi hermano llegue tarde.
yourTurn.why: A new doer needs *que* plus the wish form: *llegue*.

pitfalls.wrong: Estoy harta de que llegas tarde.
pitfalls.right: Estoy harta de que llegues tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *de que* the verb takes the wish form: *llegues*.
Almost. English likes "-ing" here, but Spanish uses the infinitive after *de*.
Almost. A feeling you are in right now takes *estar*.
